items.title: Temple brain blood-flow wearable claims draw clinical scrutiny
items.summary: Reuters reported medical experts questioning whether the temple-mounted optical device can measure brain blood flow as claimed; the founder describes Temple as a fitness/wellness product rather than a regulated medical device. The claims remain disputed and should not be presented as clinically established.
items.impact: Highlights the need for careful claims, accessible validation data, and a bright boundary between wellness and diagnosis.
items.status: Wellness claims disputed — not a verified medical approval

items.title: Aurora wearable cardiac patch reaches 800+ NOECHO study enrollees
items.summary: Skribe says its Aurora multi-sensor adhesive patch, combining ECG, phonocardiography and seismocardiography with AI to estimate left ventricular ejection fraction, is being studied in more than 800 participants across US and Southeast Asian sites. The FDA lists Aurora among READI-Home Innovation Challenge participants.
items.impact: A high-value example of developing clinical-grade cardiovascular biomarkers from multimodal wearable signals and validating them against echocardiography.
items.status: Clinical development; FDA READI-Home challenge selection only. NOT FDA-cleared or approved based on this selection.
items.source: Skribe Medical announcement; FDA READI-Home participant list

items.title: XRHealth announces acquisition of PursueCare and prescription digital therapeutics
items.summary: XRHealth announced it acquired virtual addiction-treatment provider PursueCare, bringing clinical services and FDA-authorized software therapeutics reSET and reSET-O into its wider XR/digital-care platform. This is adjacent digital therapeutics, not an acquisition of a wearable biosensor manufacturer.
items.impact: Illustrates the market for combining regulated digital therapeutics and physician services with connected devices and home-based care.
items.status: Acquisition announced as completed by buyer on November 9; financial terms not disclosed in company release.

items.title: SPADE optoacoustic miniature sensor explores continuous cuffless blood-pressure estimation
items.summary: Technion researchers report a silicon-photonics/optoacoustic device using short light pulses to generate acoustic signals from arteries. A single miniature sensor estimates vessel diameter and beat-to-beat changes, which can support pressure waveform modelling. Announced November 9 and covered again November 10–11.
items.impact: Potential future component for compact wearable BP monitoring; validate across individuals, movement and daily settings before clinical use.
items.status: Peer-reviewed early proof of concept; not a commercial medical-device clearance.

items.company: South Korean investigators / American Heart Association
items.title: AI smartwatch ECG screening study flags reduced heart-pumping function
items.summary: Preliminary AHA 2026 research evaluated AI analysis of 30-second ECG recordings in 2,211 adults using Apple Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch. About 9% had discordant classifications between devices. In a separate home cohort, repeated positive readings reduced false positives but also missed some cases.
items.impact: Hardware/platform drift and repeated-measurement rules are important for translating consumer wearable ECG into clinically useful screening.
items.status: Conference abstract; preliminary research, not peer-reviewed full publication and not a new device approval.

items.title: WHO opens consultation on wrist-worn wearables for physical-activity surveillance
items.summary: WHO published a draft target product profile outlining minimum and enhanced requirements for wrist-worn wearables used in national and subnational physical-activity and sedentary-behaviour monitoring. Stakeholder feedback is invited through December 6, 2026.
items.impact: Provides an opportunity for wearable developers to comment on measurement accuracy, interoperability, data access and feasibility in low-resource populations.
items.status: Draft WHO product profile consultation; NOT a device approval or binding regulatory standard.

items.title: PulseAI announces FDA 510(k) clearance for wearable arrhythmia analysis
items.summary: PulseAI disclosed a U.S. FDA 510(k) clearance for its PulseAPI SmartWatch AI-powered arrhythmia analysis software; the FDA decision letter is dated October 27, 2026. This is a 510(k) clearance, not a PMA approval, and does not mean all smartwatch features are FDA-cleared.
items.impact: Indicates a pathway for clinically evaluated algorithms that interpret wearable cardiac data.
items.status: FDA 510(k) cleared · decision Oct 27

items.title: Wearable movement metrics may improve stroke recovery assessment
items.summary: NIH highlighted research on a wrist-worn tool designed to quantify recovery of arm function after a stroke, including daily-life movements that clinic assessments may miss. The research does not itself establish a cleared product.
items.impact: Shows how digital biomarkers can transform longitudinal clinical endpoints beyond consumer step counts.
items.status: Research · clinical validation needed

items.title: Nature study validates smartwatch PPG/accelerometer AI for hypertension risk screening
items.summary: A prospective 196-participant multicenter study evaluated a cuff-calibration-free AI model based on smartwatch PPG and accelerometry against 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring. Over seven days it found sensitivity 65.8% and specificity 90.0% for identifying hypertension. It estimates risk, not a continuous pressure reading.
items.impact: Important differentiation between passive screening for possible hypertension and claiming a device directly measures blood pressure.
items.status: Peer-reviewed research; not evidence of FDA approval or a replacement for cuff-based diagnosis.

items.title: FDA classifies wearable orthopedic vibration device type into Class II
items.summary: A final FDA classification order establishes Class II special controls for a wearable vibration device for orthopedic use. This is a device-type classification decision, not a blanket clearance for individual commercial products.
items.impact: A reference point for how FDA can define special controls for emerging wearable therapeutic technologies.
items.status: Class II classification order — not product approval

items.title: MIT-led team funded up to $38M for noninvasive biomarker patch
items.summary: The proposed PYTHIA wearable patch will aim to monitor biomarkers relevant to heart failure and sepsis in real time, using body heat for power. This is a funded research project, not an approved or commercially available diagnostic.
items.impact: Watch low-power multimodal biomarkers and sweat/interstitial sensing as potential next-generation platforms.
items.status: Research funding · pre-commercial

items.title: EU revises EUDAMED guidance on SS(C)P management
items.summary: An updated MDCG position paper addresses management and upload of summaries of safety and clinical performance in EUDAMED as mandatory modules roll out. This is regulatory guidance relevant to affected MDR/IVDR devices, not an individual wearable CE certificate.
items.impact: EU-bound device teams should track documentation, UDI/registration requirements and notified body obligations.
items.status: MDCG guidance revision — not product approval

items.title: Empatica launches WellPD Parkinson's monitoring wearable and app
items.summary: Empatica introduced WellPD for at-home tracking of Parkinson's motor symptoms, sleep and activity, with medication logging. The company states the offering is built on an FDA-cleared and CE-marked Parkinson's monitoring platform; the launch announcement did not establish that each feature is separately cleared.
items.impact: Condition-specific remote monitoring with clinician-oriented trends is a promising model for medical wearables.
items.status: Product launched · platform regulatory claims per company

items.title: Reference: CDSCO medical-device software guidance under MDR-2017
items.summary: CDSCO published guidance on medical-device software covering regulatory framework, classification, safety, performance, submissions, quality and post-market expectations. This July 2026 document is a background reference, NOT a new November approval or notice.
items.impact: Useful baseline when determining whether wellness analytics become regulated medical-device software in India.
items.status: Background guidance · no new approval verified
